items.note: Read right to left, the print shows ע, then a vertical stroke that reaches the baseline like ו, then א. The middle stroke could possibly be a short י, which is why confidence is low.

items.line: Sanhedrin 102, a heißt es: אין ארי דורס ונוהם, wo das Wort דורס
items.note: A small broken mark next to the נ looks like a damaged initial ו (ונוהם, 'and roars'), but it could also be a speck or stray punctuation, which would make the reading נוהם.

items.line: gelbe Feuchtigkeit (Arist. l. c. 9, 31, 3), welche ויהורא (Chulin ibid.
items.note: The first letter looks like the later ו in the same word, a plain vertical stroke without the side-projecting head of a ז, so I read ויהורא. This conflicts with the expected Talmudic term זיהרא/זיהורא, so it may be a misprint, or I may be misreading a small ז.

items.line: טגרים (Τίγρις) und umschrieben: אריא דבי עילאי „Löwe des
items.note: The last letter seems to have squared bottom corners like final mem (ם), not the rounded bottom of samekh (ס), so I read טגרים. ם and ס look very similar in this small, worn type, so this is uncertain. Also, no yod appears after the ט.

items.line: benennt ihn, wie wir gesehen, auch der Talmud neben טגרים auch
items.note: The last letter looks like a squared final mem (ם) with a flat base, not a rounded samekh (ס), so I read טגרים. The expected Greek-derived form would be טגריס. The resolution is low, so the ם/ס distinction is not certain.
